A.explanation: Too small by about a factor of 4, obtained if the diameter $0.25\text{ mm}$ is mistakenly used as the radius when calculating $A = \pi r^2$.

B.explanation: Too small, obtained if the total scale reading of about $8.0\text{ mm}$ is used as the extension instead of the change in reading of about $3.5\text{ mm}$.

C.explanation: Too small, obtained from a misread extension or area, for example using $\Delta x \approx 4.7\text{ mm}$ instead of the correct $3.5\text{ mm}$ change from the $F$ against marker position graph.

D.explanation: Correct from $E = FL/(A\Delta x)$ with $L = 3.70\text{ m}$, $A$ from $d = 0.25\text{ mm}$, and $\Delta x \approx 3.5\text{ mm}$ for $\Delta F = 10\text{ N}$, giving about $2.2 \times 10^{11}\text{ Pa}$.

hints: Notice the vertical axis is marker position on scale in $\text{mm}$, not extension, so find the change in reading between $F = 0$ and $F = 10\text{ N}$ to get $\Delta x$.
Recall Young modulus as $E = \text{stress}/\text{strain} = FL/(A\Delta x)$ with tested length $L = 3.70\text{ m}$ and area $A = \pi d^2/4$ from diameter $0.25\text{ mm}$.

Calculate $A$ in $\text{m}^2$ and $\Delta x/\Delta F$ in $\text{m N}^{-1}$ from the straight-line gradient, then evaluate $E = (L/A) \times (\Delta F/\Delta x)$ and check the power of ten in $\text{Pa}$.
walkthrough: Identify the tested length and wire size: $L = 3.70\text{ m}$ between clamp and marker, and $d = 0.25\text{ mm} = 2.5 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}$.

Read extension from the graph of marker position against $F$: at $F = 0$, position is about $4.5\text{ mm}$ and at $F = 10\text{ N}$, position is about $8.0\text{ mm}$, so $\Delta x \approx 3.5\text{ mm} = 3.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}$ for $\Delta F = 10\text{ N}$.
State the rule: $E = \text{stress}/\text{strain} = (F/A)/(\Delta x/L) = F L/(A \Delta x)$.
This matches the value $2.2 \times 10^{11}\text{ Pa}$. This is option D.
